quests.instruction: Read the passage and decide if the statement is true or false.
quests.passage: Halima wakes up at 6 a.m. every day, even on weekends. She says the early start gives her quiet time to read before work.
quests.question: Halima gets up early on Saturdays and Sundays too.
quests.hint: Read the phrase after "every day."
quests.explanation: "Even on weekends" means Saturdays and Sundays are included.
quests.evidenceLine: Halima wakes up at 6 a.m. every day, even on weekends.

quests.instruction: Read the passage and decide if the statement is true or false.
quests.passage: Drinking enough water helps the body stay cool and think clearly. Most adults need about two liters of water each day, but people who exercise may need more.
quests.question: Adults who exercise may need more than two liters of water a day.
quests.hint: Look at what changes for people who exercise.
quests.explanation: The passage says people who exercise may need more than the usual two liters.
quests.evidenceLine: Most adults need about two liters of water each day, but people who exercise may need more.

quests.instruction: Read the passage and decide if the statement is true or false.
quests.passage: A traditional Indian thali comes with rice, bread, lentils, and vegetables. Small steel bowls hold each dish, so the flavors of the different foods do not mix.
quests.question: In a thali, the different foods are kept in separate bowls.
quests.hint: Find how the dishes are served.
quests.explanation: Small bowls hold each dish, so the foods stay apart.
quests.evidenceLine: Small steel bowls hold each dish, so the flavors of the different foods do not mix.

quests.instruction: Read the passage and decide if the statement is true or false.
quests.passage: Plants make their own food using sunlight, water, and air. This process happens mostly in the green leaves, which is why leaves are so important to a plant.
quests.question: Plants make most of their food in their roots.
quests.hint: Where does the process happen?
quests.explanation: Food is made mostly in the green leaves, not in the roots.
quests.evidenceLine: This process happens mostly in the green leaves, which is why leaves are so important to a plant.

quests.instruction: Read the passage and decide if the statement is true or false.
quests.passage: Mr. Evans divides his class into groups of four for science projects. There are twenty-four students in his class, and each group chooses its own topic.
quests.question: There are six groups in Mr. Evans's class.
quests.hint: Think about how many groups of four you can make.
quests.explanation: Twenty-four students in groups of four make six groups.
quests.evidenceLine: Mr. Evans divides his class into groups of four for science projects. There are twenty-four students in his class, and each group chooses its own topic.

quests.instruction: Read the passage and decide if the statement is true or false.
quests.passage: Dogs sweat very little through their skin. Instead, they cool down by panting with their tongues out, which helps heat leave the body.
quests.question: Dogs cool down mainly by sweating through their skin.
quests.hint: How do dogs get rid of heat?
quests.explanation: Dogs pant because they sweat very little, so skin sweat is not their main method.
quests.evidenceLine: Instead, they cool down by panting with their tongues out, which helps heat leave the body.

quests.instruction: Read the passage and decide if the statement is true or false.
quests.passage: Beatriz writes down three things she is thankful for before she goes to sleep. She started this habit a year ago and has not missed a single night since.
quests.question: Beatriz has kept her habit going every night for a year.
quests.hint: Look at how long the habit has lasted and whether she missed any nights.
quests.explanation: She began a year ago and has missed no nights, so she has done it nightly for a year.
quests.evidenceLine: She started this habit a year ago and has not missed a single night since.

quests.instruction: Read the passage and decide if the statement is true or false.
quests.passage: In Thailand, people usually take off their shoes before entering a home. Visitors who forget are gently reminded at the door, and nobody feels embarrassed.
quests.question: Guests in a Thai home are expected to remove their shoes.
quests.hint: Notice the expected behavior at the door.
quests.explanation: People usually take off their shoes before going in, and forgetful visitors get a reminder.
quests.evidenceLine: In Thailand, people usually take off their shoes before entering a home.

quests.instruction: Read the passage and decide if the statement is true or false.
quests.passage: The new coffee shop on Elm Street opened two weeks ago. It is busiest in the morning when office workers stop by, and it is nearly empty after 2 p.m.
quests.question: The coffee shop is busiest in the afternoon.
quests.hint: When is the coffee shop busiest?
quests.explanation: It is busiest in the morning and nearly empty after 2 p.m.
quests.evidenceLine: It is busiest in the morning when office workers stop by, and it is nearly empty after 2 p.m.

quests.instruction: Read the passage and decide if the statement is true or false.
quests.passage: For this recipe, cook the pasta for ten minutes. Then drain it, add the sauce, and serve it right away while it is still hot.
quests.question: The sauce is added before the pasta is cooked.
quests.hint: Put the recipe steps in order.
quests.explanation: The pasta is cooked first, and the sauce goes on after draining.
quests.evidenceLine: For this recipe, cook the pasta for ten minutes. Then drain it, add the sauce, and serve it right away while it is still hot.

quests.instruction: Read the passage and decide if the statement is true or false.
quests.passage: The school year at Nova School begins in September and ends in June. Students also get a two-week holiday in December, and another one in the spring.
quests.question: Nova School students have more than one holiday during the school year.
quests.hint: Count the holidays mentioned.
quests.explanation: They get a holiday in December and another in spring, which is two holidays.
quests.evidenceLine: Students also get a two-week holiday in December, and another one in the spring.

quests.instruction: Read the passage and decide if the statement is true or false.
quests.passage: Tickets to the science museum cost $10 for adults and $5 for children. Children under three enter for free, and members never pay for a ticket.
quests.question: A two-year-old must pay $5 to enter.
quests.hint: Who gets in for free?
quests.explanation: Children under three enter free, and a two-year-old is under three.
quests.evidenceLine: Children under three enter for free, and members never pay for a ticket.

quests.instruction: Read the passage and decide if the statement is true or false.
quests.passage: Rashid's job is to check the quality of shoes at a factory. He looks closely at each pair and puts the ones with mistakes in a red box.
quests.question: Rashid separates shoes that have mistakes from good ones.
quests.hint: Focus on how Rashid handles the pairs with mistakes.
quests.explanation: The pairs with mistakes go into the red box, apart from the good pairs.
quests.evidenceLine: He looks closely at each pair and puts the ones with mistakes in a red box.

quests.instruction: Read the passage and decide if the statement is true or false.
quests.passage: Long ago, sailors used the stars to find their way at sea. Today most ships use satellites and computers to know where they are.
quests.question: Most ships today depend on the stars to find their way.
quests.hint: Compare what sailors used long ago with what ships use now.
quests.explanation: Today most ships use satellites and computers rather than the stars.
quests.evidenceLine: Today most ships use satellites and computers to know where they are.

quests.instruction: Read the passage and decide if the statement is true or false.
quests.passage: The city theater will show a new play every month this year. Tickets for each play go on sale two weeks before the first show.
quests.question: Tickets go on sale after a play has already opened.
quests.hint: Which comes first, the ticket sale or the first show?
quests.explanation: Tickets go on sale two weeks before the first show, so they are sold earlier.
quests.evidenceLine: Tickets for each play go on sale two weeks before the first show.

quests.instruction: Read the passage and decide if the statement is true or false.
quests.passage: Learning a new language is easier if you practice a little every day. Thirty minutes daily works better than studying for three hours once a week.
quests.question: Short daily practice is better than one long lesson each week.
quests.hint: Compare thirty minutes a day with three hours once a week.
quests.explanation: The passage says the daily habit works better than one long weekly session.
quests.evidenceLine: Thirty minutes daily works better than studying for three hours once a week.

quests.instruction: Read the passage and decide if the statement is true or false.
quests.passage: Malik has a cold, so his doctor told him to stay home for two days. He should rest, drink plenty of water, and avoid going to work until he feels better.
quests.question: Malik should stay away from work until he feels better.
quests.hint: Reread the doctor's advice about work.
quests.explanation: The doctor told him to avoid going to work until he feels better.
quests.evidenceLine: He should rest, drink plenty of water, and avoid going to work until he feels better.

quests.instruction: Read the passage and decide if the statement is true or false.
quests.passage: The evening news starts at 6:30 p.m. and lasts thirty minutes. A weather report follows immediately after it, and then a game show begins at seven.
quests.question: The weather report comes before the news.
quests.hint: Which comes first after 6:30 p.m., the news or the weather?
quests.explanation: The weather report follows the news, so it does not come before it.
quests.evidenceLine: A weather report follows immediately after it, and then a game show begins at seven.

quests.instruction: Read the passage and decide if the statement is true or false.
quests.passage: Sound moves through air, but it moves faster through water. That is one reason whales can hear each other from very far away in the ocean.
quests.question: Sound travels more quickly in water than in air.
quests.hint: Which is faster, sound in air or sound in water?
quests.explanation: The passage says sound moves faster through water than through air.
quests.evidenceLine: Sound moves through air, but it moves faster through water.

quests.instruction: Read the passage and decide if the statement is true or false.
quests.passage: In a basketball game, each team has five players on the court. A game is played in four quarters of ten minutes each, with a short break between them.
quests.question: Each team has six players on the court.
quests.hint: Find the number of players.
quests.explanation: Each team has five players on the court, not six.
quests.evidenceLine: In a basketball game, each team has five players on the court.

quests.instruction: Read the passage and decide if the statement is true or false.
quests.passage: The hotel offers a free shuttle bus to the airport every hour. Guests must reserve a seat at the front desk the night before they travel.
quests.question: Guests need to reserve their shuttle seat in advance.
quests.hint: Look for the step guests must take before traveling.
quests.explanation: Guests must reserve a seat the night before, which means booking in advance.
quests.evidenceLine: Guests must reserve a seat at the front desk the night before they travel.

quests.instruction: Read the passage and decide if the statement is true or false.
quests.passage: It rains almost every afternoon in the rainforest. Mornings are usually dry and bright, and the sun is already strong by ten o'clock.
quests.question: Mornings are the rainiest time of day in the rainforest.
quests.hint: When does it rain in the rainforest?
quests.explanation: It rains in the afternoons, and mornings are usually dry.
quests.evidenceLine: It rains almost every afternoon in the rainforest. Mornings are usually dry and bright, and the sun is already strong by ten o'clock.

quests.instruction: Read the passage and decide if the statement is true or false.
quests.passage: Eun-ji and her roommate share a two-bedroom apartment in the city. They split the rent equally, so each of them pays $450 a month.
quests.question: The total rent for the apartment is $450 a month.
quests.hint: Think about how many people share the rent.
quests.explanation: Each roommate pays $450, so the total for two people is $900.
quests.evidenceLine: They split the rent equally, so each of them pays $450 a month.

quests.instruction: Read the passage and decide if the statement is true or false.
quests.passage: Fewer people in the village now drive to the market. Two years ago, the village started a free bicycle-sharing program, and many neighbors use it every day.
quests.question: The village lets people borrow bicycles at no cost.
quests.hint: Read about the program the village started.
quests.explanation: A free bicycle-sharing program means people can borrow bikes without paying.
quests.evidenceLine: Two years ago, the village started a free bicycle-sharing program, and many neighbors use it every day.

quests.instruction: Read the passage and decide if the statement is true or false.
quests.passage: Tomato plants need at least six hours of sun each day. Petra's garden gets only three hours of sun, so her tomatoes grow slowly.
quests.question: Petra's tomato plants get enough sun.
quests.hint: Compare the sun the plants need with the sun the garden gets.
quests.explanation: Tomatoes need six hours, but the garden gets only three.
quests.evidenceLine: Tomato plants need at least six hours of sun each day. Petra's garden gets only three hours of sun, so her tomatoes grow slowly.

quests.instruction: Read the passage and decide if the statement is true or false.
quests.passage: Mobile phones use less battery when the screen is dim. Tarek turns down his brightness every night, and now his phone lasts a whole day.
quests.question: Tarek's phone does not last a whole day now.
quests.hint: Consider the effect of the dimmer screen.
quests.explanation: After dimming the screen, his phone lasts a whole day.
quests.evidenceLine: Tarek turns down his brightness every night, and now his phone lasts a whole day.

quests.instruction: Read the passage and decide if the statement is true or false.
quests.passage: If you smell gas in your home, do not turn on any lights. Open the windows, leave the building, and call the gas company from outside.
quests.question: You should call the gas company after leaving the building.
quests.hint: Notice the order of the actions.
quests.explanation: The steps are to open the windows, leave, and then call from outside.
quests.evidenceLine: Open the windows, leave the building, and call the gas company from outside.

quests.instruction: Read the passage and decide if the statement is true or false.
quests.passage: Elephants live in family groups led by the oldest female. The younger animals follow her when the group travels long distances to find water.
quests.question: An elephant family follows its oldest female.
quests.hint: Who is in charge of the group?
quests.explanation: The oldest female leads, and the younger animals follow her.
quests.evidenceLine: Elephants live in family groups led by the oldest female.

quests.instruction: Read the passage and decide if the statement is true or false.
quests.passage: Ruth and her cousins meet at their aunt's house every December. The aunt cooks a big dinner, and everyone helps to wash the dishes afterward.
quests.question: The cousins gather at Ruth's house.
quests.hint: Whose house do the cousins meet at?
quests.explanation: They meet at their aunt's house, not at Ruth's.
quests.evidenceLine: Ruth and her cousins meet at their aunt's house every December.

quests.instruction: Read the passage and decide if the statement is true or false.
quests.passage: The new sports center will open in the north of the city in May. It will have two swimming pools and a running track, and parking will be free.
quests.question: The sports center will have three swimming pools.
quests.hint: Count the swimming pools.
quests.explanation: The center will have two pools, not three.
quests.evidenceLine: It will have two swimming pools and a running track, and parking will be free.
